finding: SI 4/2020 regulation 3(4) places the pest-risk analysis after receipt of the permit application for an in-scope plant product; it is not a published automatic no-document processing exemption. Neither that procedure nor the separate trade licence list identifies manufactured sencha as outside scope. No new national ISPM32 commodity adoption/list was located in this targeted review.

National procedure PR01-23 section 4 lists NIMP 5 and NIMP 32 as reference documents. It contains no operative clause adopting a particular low-risk category as a permit/certificate exemption. Section 3.2 compares origin pests with the national quarantine list after the application; section 3.3 still specifies origin phytosanitary or disinsection documentation. No new national classification settling steamed sencha was located.

The 2017 WTO review Table 3.5 expressly associates the general plants/plant-products category with prior agricultural authorization and origin phytosanitary certification. Its stated exceptions concern active substances in phytopharmaceutical products, not processed food. Section 3.38 likewise gives a general SPS-certificate account. These corroborate the controlled pathway but do not classify sencha under the national simple-preparation definition or supply a personal-post exemption. No new current national commodity list was found.
